h1:
5 Affordable Short-Stay Hotels
Sukhumvit Bangkok
Great Value · Bookable Online · Honest Reviews
heroSub: Five well-reviewed hotels along Sukhumvit that work equally well for a full overnight or a daytime short stay. Four officially accept day-use bookings via Dayuse.com — clean rooms, standard check-in, no awkward atmosphere. Starting from ฿700/night.
introH2: What is day-use, and how does it work at a real Bangkok hotel?
introHtml: Day-use is a service offered officially by 3- and 4-star hotels, booked in advance through Dayuse.com. You pick your date and time window, pay online with a credit card, and check in at the front desk like any regular guest — then use your room plus facilities such as a rooftop pool or gym, and check out by early evening. There is a full digital receipt, no awkward conversation, and no difference in how the room looks or smells from a normal overnight. This guide covers 5 Sukhumvit hotels we have reviewed in depth, each backed by real guest reviews. Four accept day-use online; all five work equally well for a budget overnight. Prices compared across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com.
mrtHtml: The five hotels span Sukhumvit from Soi 8 near BTS Nana, through Soi 13 and 15 near Asok, to Soi 71 in Ekkamai (free shuttle to BTS Phra Khanong/Ekkamai), and finally Soi 52 at On Nut. The BTS Sukhumvit Line (dark green) connects every point — Siam, Terminal 21 and Emporium are all a few stops away. Transfer to the Airport Rail Link at Phaya Thai for Suvarnabhumi Airport.

entries.storyHtml: Night Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit 15 has the highest review volume in this list — 4,380 reviews at 8.7 on Booking.com — and two things come up again and again: the rooftop pool with jacuzzi (quiet, good views) and staff who reviewers consistently describe as going out of their way to help. Day-use is bookable via Dayuse.com at around US$46, including pool and jacuzzi access; check-in is exactly like a normal guest. A free hotel tuk-tuk runs to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit throughout the day, and Terminal 21 is about 450 m on foot. The honest caveats: the hotel has two buildings — some rooms require a short road-crossing to reach the pool (ask at check-in), and the mattresses are very soft, which not everyone likes.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: book day-use on Dayuse.com in advance — slots are limited per day. Ask which building your room is in if pool proximity matters. The Flava breakfast buffet earns consistent praise; worth adding if available as a package.

entries.storyHtml: Citrus Sukhumvit 13 Nana Bangkok (Compass Hospitality, 79 rooms) was fully renovated in late 2024–early 2025, and post-renovation reviews are unanimous: rooms are clean, bright and better than the price suggests. Booking.com 8.6 from 1,778 reviews. Day-use is bookable via Dayuse.com, window 10:00–18:00, including rooftop pool access — standard check-in, no fuss. A free tuk-tuk shuttle runs to BTS Nana, BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit, which takes care of the 650 m gap to the nearest station. The honest caveats: the entry-level Premier Room at 22 sqm is snug for two people with luggage — upgrade to a Corner Room if that matters. The in-house restaurant has a limited menu.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: book day-use via Dayuse.com in advance; free cancellation available. Use the free hotel shuttle instead of walking in midday Bangkok heat. Two people with luggage should choose the 28 sqm Premier Corner Room.

entries.storyHtml: lyf Sukhumvit 8 Bangkok — lyf brand by The Ascott Limited, opened 2022, 196 studio rooms — ranks third on two advantages that are hard to beat: roughly 2–3 min walk to BTS Nana (approximately 180–200 m), the shortest in this list, and the cheapest official day-use at around $29 (56% off) via Dayuse.com, including the room, communal kitchen, co-working lounge and Wi-Fi. Ascott standards keep cleanliness high and design is sharp. The honest caveats: rooms are a compact 16 sqm with no in-room fridge (use the shared BOND kitchen) and thin walls that carry noise from neighbouring rooms. Adults-only (18+) — no children whatsoever.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: book day-use via Dayuse.com at $29 — cheapest in this list. Request a higher floor and an inner-facing room if you sleep lightly; Soi 8 has a lively nightlife scene. The standard room has no TV; upgrade to a Plus room for ฿200–400 more.

entries.storyHtml: Somerset Sukhumvit 71 Bangkok is the premium day-use pick in this list — a 4-star Ascott serviced apartment opened late 2024 on Sukhumvit 71 in Ekkamai. Everything is brand new. The headline feature is a 15th-floor infinity pool with Sol & Luna restaurant and 360-degree city views — mentioned in virtually every review. Day-use starts at around ฿1,400 via Dayuse.com (58% off the overnight rate), fully bookable online with a receipt, covering the room, pool and gym. The honest caveats: it is not within walking distance of BTS — a free hotel shuttle or Grab (~10 min) is needed for both BTS Phra Khanong and Ekkamai. Sound insulation between rooms is thin, which several reviewers flag; a corner room or higher floor helps.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: day-use must be booked directly via Dayuse.com, not through Agoda or Booking.com. Arrive at Sol & Luna around 5–7 pm for the best golden-hour city views. Request a corner room or high floor if noise sensitivity is a concern.

entries.storyHtml: Let us be upfront about Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station: it does not offer day-use — overnight stays only (check-in 2 pm, check-out noon). It is also in outer Sukhumvit at On Nut, not the Nana/Asok neighbourhood. But if your question is simply "what is the cleanest, best-located overnight hotel for ฿700 in this part of Bangkok?" the answer is clear. Booking.com 8.8 from 957 reviews (tied for highest score in this list). Opened in 2022, everything is still fresh. All rooms have a private balcony, fridge, air-con, flat-screen TV, free Wi-Fi and free parking. BTS On Nut is 260 m away — roughly 3 minutes on foot. From there you can reach Thong Lo, Ekkamai or Terminal 21 in a few stops. The honest caveat: amenities are intentionally minimal — no shampoo, toothbrush, hair dryer or in-room kettle. Pack your own or buy from the 7-Eleven downstairs.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: bring your own toiletries — Hop Inn provides soap and shower gel only. If you need a day-use short stay instead, look at hotels 1–3 in this list. BTS On Nut also connects to Suvarnabhumi Airport via the Airport Rail Link at Makkasan/Phaya Thai.

faqTitle: FAQ — Short-Stay & Day-Use Hotels in Sukhumvit Bangkok

faq.q: Is day-use at a Bangkok hotel legal and normal?
faq.a: Yes, entirely legal and increasingly mainstream. Day-use is a service offered officially by 3- and 4-star hotels through Dayuse.com. You book online, pay by card, receive a digital receipt, and check in at the front desk like any regular guest. There is no difference in the room or facilities — you just check out before early evening instead of the next morning. No awkward questions, no different atmosphere.

faq.q: Which hotel in this list has the cheapest day-use?
faq.a: lyf Sukhumvit 8 Bangkok is the cheapest at around $29 (approximately 56% off the overnight rate) via Dayuse.com. The package includes the room, Wi-Fi, communal kitchen and co-working lounge. It also has the best BTS access in the list at just 2–3 minutes walk to BTS Nana.

faq.q: Which hotels here have a rooftop pool AND accept day-use bookings?
faq.a: Two hotels in the Nana/Asok corridor offer both: Night Hotel Sukhumvit 15 with a rooftop pool and jacuzzi (day-use ~US$46) and Citrus Sukhumvit 13 with a rooftop pool (day-use 10 am–6 pm). Somerset Sukhumvit 71 also has a 15th-floor infinity pool and day-use (฿1,400) but is further out in Ekkamai and requires a shuttle.

faq.q: How do I book a day-use session online?
faq.a: Go to Dayuse.com, search the hotel name (Night Hotel Bangkok, Citrus Sukhumvit 13, lyf Sukhumvit 8, or Somerset Sukhumvit 71), pick your date and time window, pay with a credit card, and receive a confirmation email. On the day, check in at the hotel front desk exactly as a normal guest would. Free cancellation is usually available within a set window.

faq.q: What is the difference between day-use and an hourly short-stay room?
faq.a: They are fundamentally different. Day-use at a 3- or 4-star hotel is booked through a legitimate online platform, has a full paper trail, uses the exact same room as overnight guests, includes facilities like pools and gyms, and involves a normal front-desk check-in. A traditional hourly room typically has no online booking, cash only, and a very different atmosphere.

faq.q: I just need the cheapest clean overnight stay near BTS — which do I pick?
faq.a: Hop Inn Bangkok Onnut Station — from ฿700/night, 8.8 on Booking.com, 3-minute walk to BTS On Nut, free parking, private balcony in every room, opened 2022. Note: no day-use, minimal toiletries (bring your own), and it is in outer Sukhumvit at On Nut rather than the central Nana/Asok area.
